title: DSW-1605: four-input and seven-input dissection with measured windows, S_C = O(2^((3/5) sqrt n)), T = Q = O(2^((321/200) sqrt n)), O(n) qubits

claims.statement: For every N >= 2 and every s in Z/NZ, with n = ceil(log2 N), the single DSW-1605 algorithm and configuration of proof.md (finite exhaustive branch for n < 2^28; otherwise r0 = ceil(sqrt n), t = floor(1999 r0/10000), w = 3t, y7 = ceil(r0/10), a collimation tree of binary levels, then four-input levels, then seven-input levels, both with measured windows and listed by a guess-and-chunk dissection, with tables of at most about 2^w entries, the free-frequency odd-part decoder and the controlled-shift 2-adic part) outputs the entire s with unconditional probability at least 1 - 2^-8 > 2/3 from independent ideal coset copies, and on EVERY execution branch, including all failures, discards and aborts, its total charged sequential work is T(N,s) = O(2^((321/200) sqrt n)), with an absolute constant. The stronger main-branch bound is T = O(n^7 2^(1.6002 sqrt n)). The uniform bit-length envelope B_T(n) = 2^((321/200) sqrt n) has growth index exactly 1/2. This holds jointly with the classical-memory, quantum-memory and sample bounds of the other claims.

For the same DSW-1605 algorithm and configuration of proof.md, for every N >= 2 and every s in Z/NZ, with n = ceil(log2 N), peak classical memory on every execution branch is S_C(N,s) = O(2^((3/5) sqrt n)) bits, with an absolute constant, including depth-first merge tables, enumeration chunks and decoder records. The stronger main-branch bound is S_C = O(n^2 2^(0.5997 sqrt n)). The envelope B_C(n) = 2^((3/5) sqrt n) has growth index exactly 1/2. This holds jointly with the stated work, quantum-memory and sample bounds and full-secret success probability at least 1 - 2^-8.

For the same DSW-1605 algorithm and configuration of proof.md, for every N >= 2 and every s in Z/NZ, with n = ceil(log2 N), peak quantum memory on every execution branch is S_Q(N,s) = O(n) qubits, with an absolute constant, including the depth-first index registers and all ancillas. The envelope B_Q(n) = n has growth index exactly 0. This holds jointly with the stated work, classical-memory and sample bounds and full-secret success probability at least 1 - 2^-8.

For the same DSW-1605 algorithm and configuration of proof.md, for every N >= 2 and every s in Z/NZ, with n = ceil(log2 N), the total number Q(N,s) of fresh DCP source copies acquired on every execution branch, including every discarded copy and every failed or aborted attempt, is O(2^((321/200) sqrt n)), with an absolute constant. The stronger main-branch bound is Q <= n Ccap + K = O(n^3 2^(1.6002 sqrt n)), with Ccap and K defined in proof.md. The uniform bit-length envelope B_samples(n) = 2^((321/200) sqrt n) has growth index exactly 1/2. This holds jointly with the stated work and memory bounds and unconditional full-secret success probability at least 1 - 2^-8.

For the same DSW-1605 algorithm and configuration of proof.md, the proved fractional error tolerance is epsilon(n) = 0: all Q source copies are independent ideal coset states. Under this promise, for every N and s, full-secret recovery succeeds with probability at least 1 - 2^-8 jointly with all four resource bounds. No positive corruption tolerance is asserted; this is not a proof that greater tolerance is impossible.

structured.error_model: Malformed fraction among acquired copies. The proved guarantee requires every copy to be an independent ideal coset state; no behavior is promised for malformed copies.
